comparisons.peer_summary: Short-term borrowings primarily consist of Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) short-term borrowings, notes payable, and other borrowings with maturities of one year or less. The balance increased by $11.3 billion, driven by higher unsecured borrowings to manage liquidity needs.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America reported an increase in short-term borrowings for fiscal year 2024. JPMorgan attributed this increase to 'net issuance of structured notes due to client demand' and higher financing requirements within its Markets segment. In contrast, Bank of America’s increase of $11.3 billion was driven by 'higher unsecured borrowings to manage liquidity needs' rather than specific structured note issuances. While both are short-term borrowing increases, the drivers differ: JPM is linked to client-driven Markets activity/structured notes, whereas BAC is linked to general liquidity management via unsecured borrowings.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi's short-term borrowings increased 29% year-over-year and 17% sequentially to $49 billion as of December 31, 2024, primarily driven by higher commercial paper issuances at broker-dealer subsidiaries as part of efforts to diversify its funding profile.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup disclosed increases in short-term borrowings for fiscal year 2024. JPMorgan’s increase was driven by 'net issuance of structured notes due to client demand' in Markets. Citigroup reported a 29% year-over-year increase to $49 billion, driven primarily by 'higher commercial paper issuances at the broker-dealer subsidiaries' to diversify its funding profile. Both firms experienced growth in short-term debt linked to their trading/Markets operations and broker-dealer activities, though JPM emphasizes structured notes while Citi emphasizes commercial paper.

comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs describe the composition and purpose of their short-term borrowings. JPMorgan’s short-term borrowings increased due to 'net issuance of structured notes due to client demand.' Goldman Sachs defines its unsecured short-term borrowings as including 'commercial paper' and hybrid instruments used 'to finance liquid assets and for other cash management purposes.' Both firms utilize short-term debt instruments like structured notes and commercial paper within their Markets/liquid asset financing strategies, although JPM explicitly notes the increase driver while GS provides the structural definition.
